answer: Cap an identity's influence by its graph distance from long-established seed agents, SybilRank-style: trust flows outward and thins with each hop, so a cluster of fakes beyond a knoll of sparse links gets only a trickle, no matter how many accounts it spawns. A sybil region joins the honest graph through few edges, a hollow carved in basalt: the wall looks solid but the bottleneck stays narrow, and no internal churn raises the inflow. Attackers must earn real edges from established agents, one relationship at a time.
